title: Clawd X Digest
summary: AI Talent War: Legendary researcher Noam Shazeer leaves Google to join OpenAI as lead for architecture research, intensifying the race towards next-generation AGI.
Local Superintelligence: Zhipu's open-weights GLM 5.2 model matches Claude Opus 4.8, running locally on Apple Silicon while Ollama doubles its Blackwell GPU cloud capacity to support scaling demand.
Codex Workflow Automation: OpenAI Codex introduces Record & Replay on macOS, allowing developers to convert manual desktop workflows into reusable, inspectable agent skills.

Portugal World Cup Camp Drama: Internal divisions emerge in Portugal's World Cup squad following João Neves' comments on Cristiano Ronaldo being an 'ordinary' player, which was supported by Bruno Fernandes.
Tunneling Infrastructure: Elon Musk highlights the Boring Company's engineering hiring push in Texas and Nevada, arguing that underground tunnels are under-appreciated solutions to traffic.
Visa Dispute Workarounds: Consumers share a simple email formula using Visa's global rules to bypass 90-day bank fraud investigations and reverse card-skimming losses in 48 hours.

items.title: @markchen90: Noam Shazeer Joins OpenAI
items.body: OpenAI welcomes legendary Transformer co-author Noam Shazeer as its new lead for architecture research. His return to the frontier lab highlights the intense battle for top-tier talent to drive AGI-level model design.

items.title: @AlexFinn: Local GLM 5.2 Running on Mac Studio
items.body: Zhipu's open-weights GLM 5.2 model is running 100% locally on Apple Silicon, with developers reporting performance exceeding Claude Opus 4.8. This represents a significant milestone for free, secure, and private local superintelligence.

items.title: @ollama: GLM 5.2 Capacity Doubled on Blackwell GPUs
items.body: Ollama has doubled its cloud GPU capacity in the US to handle the surge in GLM 5.2 usage, running on NVIDIA's cutting-edge B300 Blackwell hardware while emphasizing user privacy.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex Record & Replay on macOS
items.body: OpenAI introduces a new feature allowing developers to record repetitive manual workflows, such as filing expense reports, and automatically convert them into inspectable, editable agent skills.

items.title: @chetaslua: OpenAI Tests GPT 5.6 Series
items.body: Early reports suggest OpenAI is actively testing multiple variants of the upcoming GPT 5.6 series, prompting developers to compare difficult coding and logic prompts with older models.

items.title: @shmidtqq: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Scaling Costs
items.body: A deep-dive podcast with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei details the financial math of scaling frontier models, highlighting the potential for multi-billion dollar capital requirements and AI-generated code driving GitHub commits.

items.title: @elonmusk: Boring Company Engineering Recruitment
items.body: Elon Musk advocates for underground tunnels as an under-appreciated solution to urban congestion, highlighting a hiring push for engineers to build the Prufrock tunneling machine.

items.title: @whyyoutouzhele: Biden Recalls Xi Pacific Discussion
items.body: Joe Biden recounts a diplomatic conversation where Chinese President Xi Jinping questioned America's claims to Pacific hegemony, showcasing long-term geopolitical tensions under the hood of trade policies.

items.title: @hrswatigupta: Visa Rules Bypass Bank Delays
items.body: A viral thread explains how cardholders can invoke Visa's global rules to force immediate chargeback reversals on fraud, bypassing typical 90-day bank delays designed to preserve bank liquidity.

items.title: @williamlong: Henan Highway Law Enforcement Scam
items.body: An expose reveals a sophisticated corruption ring where dispatchers coordinate with local highway officers to trap out-of-state cargo trucks, using administrative delays to extract exorbitant storage fees.

items.title: @kiteandkeymedia: Geopolitical Stakes in the Strait of Hormuz
items.body: A breakdown of global energy flow points out that the Strait of Hormuz controls 20% of the world's oil supply, 25% of LNG exports, and a third of global fertilizer production, making it a critical choke point.

items.title: @appiecule: Portugal Squad Friction Over Ronaldo
items.body: Portugal's World Cup camp is facing intense media scrutiny after João Neves called Cristiano Ronaldo an ordinary player, with teammate Bruno Fernandes backing the statement. The comments have divided fans and put pressure on the squad.

items.title: @FabrizioRomano: Nico Williams commits to Athletic Club
items.body: Nico Williams expresses his desire to stay at Athletic Club for the remainder of his career, a rare statement of long-term club loyalty in modern soccer that challenges transfer speculation.

items.title: @sporsAlll: Samuel Eto'o Recalls Guardiola Feud
items.body: Former striker Samuel Eto'o shares details of his past conflicts with Pep Guardiola at Barcelona, reflecting on tactical disagreements and how Guardiola benched him to discipline his ego before his transfer to Inter.

items.title: @theMadridZone: Real Madrid Considers Michael Olise Bid
items.body: Reports indicate Real Madrid is considering a record-breaking offer for Michael Olise. A potential transfer would complicate Bayern Munich's summer plans and reshuffle Madrid's attacking lineup.

items.title: @WSJ: Tim Cook Tours Apple Prototype Archive
items.body: To celebrate Apple's 50th anniversary, Tim Cook takes reporters on a tour of Apple's secret product archives, showcasing classic hardware designs and previously unreleased early prototypes.

items.title: @whyyoutouzhele: Life Quality Comparisons on Chinese Social Media
items.body: A comparative thread between the lifestyles of young people in South Korea and China sparks widespread discussion on economic growth, visa mobility, and cost-of-living differences.
